column1: # The recall miss table (bead tla-1sh7.3, epic tla-1sh7).
# A wrong answer somebody actually writes, and what that answer says. 30 rows
# over 30 of the 120 reps in recall/REPS.tsv, reaching 25 of the 37 constructs.
# Rows are tab-delimited and carry the literal first field MISS, so prose in
# this file can never be read as data. Four fields, in order:
#   1  marker       the literal MISS
#   2  rep id       a REP row in recall/REPS.tsv
#   3  wrong        the wrong answer, as TLA+, verbatim
#   4  explanation  what that answer says
#   awk -F'\t' '$1 == "MISS" && $2 == "R107"' recall/MISSES.tsv
#   grep '^MISS' recall/MISSES.tsv | cut -f2
# Read rows with awk -F'\t' or cut, never with IFS=$'\t' read. Tab is an IFS
# whitespace character, so read folds a run of tabs into one delimiter.
# FIELD 4 SAYS WHAT THE WRONG ANSWER IS, NOT WHAT TO WRITE INSTEAD. The runner
# already prints both values side by side, and drill/SHEET.md already names the
# construct's syntax, so the right answer is on screen before this file speaks.
# "You wrote one function whose value at each element is the whole set" is the
# register. "You need a function set" is not.
# EVERY FIELD 3 SCORES rc 10 THROUGH recall/recall.sh AGAINST ITS OWN REP, and
# each was watched doing it on 2026-10-16 before its row was written. An answer
# that scores 0 is not a miss. One that scores 150 never parsed, so it reports
# on the text rather than on the idea behind it, which is other feedback.
# A REP WITH NO ROW IS THE NORMAL CASE. 90 of the 120 have none. A rep that
# finds no row here falls through to the model call, which is the fourth layer
# and is safe at this rung because the answer is already on screen. Padding
# this file to reach coverage would cost that safety and buy nothing.
# WHERE THE ROWS CAME FROM. 406 of the 498 modules under drill/*/*/verify/
# carry a leading comment naming one wrong move and what it does. Those are
# construct-level explanations wearing an item's variable names, so the work
# was re-keying them to constructs and rewriting each to name no module and no
# variable. scripts/gen-misses.sh harvests the candidates by construct. It is
# an aid and not the authority, because that rewrite is a judgment.

column1: # TWELVE OF THE 37 CONSTRUCTS HAVE NO ROW, and the reasons split three ways.
# K071 RECURSIVE, K072 higher-order operator parameter, K073 LAMBDA, K075
# bracket function definition and K076 recursive function definition: the
# mistakes the drill corpus records against these do not parse. An operator
# that refers to itself with no declaration ahead of it scores 150, and so
# does a boolean expression where an operator is wanted. Measured 2026-10-16:
# LET Doubled(t) == t * 2 IN Doubled on R110 comes back 150, not 10.
# K021 LET-IN and K074 custom binary operator: value equality cannot see that
# a name was introduced, so a wrong answer against these reps is wrong about
# the body rather than about the construct. R002 carries the one row of that
# kind worth having, and it belongs to K001 for the same reason.
# K003, K005, K006, K015 and K038: I found no mistake in the drill corpus that
# these reps would catch. The near misses I tried either scored 0 against value
# equality, which means they are a correct form, or were a misreading of the
# prompt rather than a misreading of the notation.
